pieces.name: Body donation
pieces.about: Body donation, anatomical donation, or body bequest is the donation of a whole body after death for research and education. There is usually no cost to donate a body to science; donation programs will often provide a stipend and/or cover the cost of cremation or burial once a donated cadaver has served its purpose and is returned to the family for interment.

pieces.name: Bowling
pieces.about: Bowling is a target sport and recreational activity in which a player rolls a ball toward pins or another target. The term bowling usually refers to pin bowling, most commonly ten-pin bowling, though in the United Kingdom and Commonwealth countries, bowling may also refer to target bowling, such as lawn bowls. Bowling is played by 120 million people in more than 90 countries, including 70 million people in the United States alone.

pieces.name: Brave
pieces.about: Ready to face and endure danger or pain; showing courage.

pieces.name: Breast Feeding
pieces.about: Breastfeeding is the process of feeding a child breast milk, which can come from the breast or be pumped. It's considered the best source of nutrition for infants and young children, and can offer many benefits to both the baby and the mother.

pieces.name: Butterflies
pieces.about: A nectar-feeding insect with two pairs of large, typically brightly colored wings that are covered with microscopic scales. Butterflies are distinguished from moths by having clubbed or dilated antennae, holding their wings erect when at rest, and being active by day.

pieces.name: Capitalism
pieces.about: Capitalism is an economic system based on the private ownership of the means of production and their operation for profit.

pieces.name: Car accident
pieces.about: A car accident, also known as a motor vehicle collision, or car crash, occurs when a vehicle collides with another vehicle, pedestrian, animal, road debris, or other moving or stationary obstruction, such as a tree, pole or building. Traffic collisions often result in injury, disability, death, and property damage as well as financial costs to both society and the individuals involved.

pieces.name: Career
pieces.about: A person's progress or general course of action through life or through a phase of life, as in some profession or undertaking.

pieces.name: Caregiving
pieces.about: Caregiving is providing care for the daily needs of someone that is unable to care for themselves

pieces.name: Chemotherapy
pieces.about: Chemotherapy is the type of cancer treatment that uses one or more anti-cancer drugs in a standard regimen. Chemotherapy may be given with a curative intent, or it may aim only to prolong life or to reduce symptoms. Chemotherapy is one of the major categories of the medical discipline specifically devoted to pharmacotherapy for cancer, which is called medical oncology.

pieces.name: Christmas (Winter) Break
pieces.about: Christmas break, also known as winter break or holiday break, is a period of time typically observed by schools, colleges, and universities around the Christmas holiday. It usually begins a few days before Christmas Day and extends through New Year's Day or into early January. During Christmas break, students and educators are often granted time off from classes and academic responsibilities to celebrate the holiday season with their families and loved ones. It provides an opportunity for rest, relaxation, and festivities, as well as travel and vacation activities. Christmas break varies in duration depending on the educational institution and local customs, but it generally allows students and staff to recharge and enjoy the holiday season before returning to their academic pursuits.

pieces.name: Clinical trial
pieces.about: Clinical trials are a type of research that studies new tests and treatments and evaluates their effects on human health outcomes.

pieces.name: College
pieces.about: A college is an educational institution or a constituent part of one. A college may be a degree-awarding tertiary educational institution, a part of a collegiate or federal university, an institution offering vocational education, a further education institution, or a secondary school.

pieces.name: Communion
pieces.about: The term “communion” originates from the Latin word “communio,” meaning sharing or participation, reflecting the communal aspect of the ritual. It represents the sharing of the body and blood of Jesus Christ through the faithful's consumption of bread and wine or grape juice.

pieces.name: Compassion
pieces.about: Feeling for someone else’s suffering and wanting to help ease it.

pieces.name: Concentration (Attentional control)
pieces.about: The action or power of focusing one's attention or mental effort.

pieces.name: Concern for other

pieces.name: Confession

pieces.about: Confidence is a state of self-assurance, belief in one's abilities, and a sense of certainty in one's actions, decisions, and beliefs. It involves trusting in oneself and feeling capable, competent, and worthy in various situations and contexts.

pieces.name: Confusion
pieces.about: Being unable to think clearly or understand what is happening - from illness, shock, or a situation that makes no sense.

pieces.name: Cornhole (Bean bag toss)
pieces.about: Cornhole is a lawn game popular in North America in which players or teams take turns throwing fabric bean bags at an inclined board with a hole in its far end. The goal of the game is to score points by either landing a bag on the board or putting a bag through the hole.

pieces.name: Courage
pieces.about: Courage is the mental or moral strength to venture, persevere, and withstand danger, fear, or difficulty. It involves facing challenges and taking risks despite the presence of fear, uncertainty, or potential negative outcomes. Courage can manifest in various forms, from physical bravery in the face of danger to moral courage in standing up for one's beliefs or values.

pieces.name: Craft
pieces.about: A craft or trade is a pastime or an occupation that requires particular skills and knowledge of skilled work. In a historical sense, particularly the Middle Ages and earlier, the term is usually applied to people occupied in small scale production of goods, or their maintenance, for example by tinkers. The traditional term craftsman is nowadays often replaced by artisan and by craftsperson.

pieces.name: Daily Routines
pieces.about: The activities and experiences that constitute a person's normal existence.

pieces.name: Dance
pieces.about: Moving the body in rhythm to music, alone or with others.

pieces.name: Death
pieces.about: Death is the end of life; the irreversible cessation of all biological functions that sustain a living organism. The remains of a former organism normally begin to decompose shortly after death. Death eventually and inevitably occurs in all organisms.

pieces.name: Delusion
pieces.about: A fixed false belief that someone holds onto, even when presented with evidence that it's not true. Delusions are often a symptom of a disordered state of mind, and people with delusions may have difficulty distinguishing between reality and what seems real.

pieces.name: Dependability
pieces.about: The quality of being able to be relied on; trustworthiness or constancy

pieces.name: Depression
pieces.about: Depression is a mental health disorder characterized by persistent feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and a loss of interest or pleasure in activities that were once enjoyable. It can also involve changes in appetite or weight, sleep disturbances, fatigue, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, difficulty concentrating, and thoughts of death or suicide. Depression can vary in severity and duration, ranging from mild and temporary episodes to chronic and debilitating conditions. It can significantly impair daily functioning, relationships, and overall quality of life. Depression is a common and treatable condition, often requiring a combination of therapy, medication, lifestyle changes, and support from healthcare professionals and loved ones.

pieces.name: Discovery
pieces.about: Finding or learning something new - from a small personal experience to knowledge that changes how the world is understood.

pieces.about: Any harmful deviation from the normal structural or functional state of an organism, generally associated with certain signs and symptoms and differing in nature from physical injury.

pieces.name: Disease management
pieces.about: Disease management is a proactive, multidisciplinary, systematic approach to health care delivery.

pieces.name: Disinhibition
pieces.about: Disinhibition refers to the inability to withhold an inappropriate or unwanted behavior. It can refer to the production of socially inappropriate comments or actions.

pieces.name: Drawing
pieces.about: Drawing is a visual art that uses an instrument to mark paper or another two-dimensional surface. The instruments used to make a drawing are pencils, crayons, pens with inks, brushes with paints, or combinations of these, and in more modern times, computer styluses with graphics tablets or gamepads in VR drawing software.

pieces.name: Drinking alcohol
pieces.about: Drinking alcohol involves consuming beverages containing ethanol, a psychoactive substance with depressant effects on the central nervous system. Alcohol is commonly found in various types of beverages such as beer, wine, and spirits. People drink alcohol for various reasons, including socializing, relaxation, celebration, and cultural or religious practices. However, excessive or irresponsible alcohol consumption can lead to health problems, addiction, impaired judgment, and social or legal issues. It's important to consume alcohol responsibly and be aware of its potential risks and effects on personal health and well-being.

pieces.name: Drunk driving
pieces.about: Drunk driving is driving while under the influence of any substance, including alcohol, and is also known as driving under the influence (DUI). It's illegal to drive drunk in every state.

pieces.name: Early-onset Alzheimer's disease
pieces.sentence: (Page 10) The central focus of the novel, Alice Howland is diagnosed with early-onset Alzheimer’s disease at age 50. The novel explores the medical, emotional, and psychological aspects of living with Alzheimer’s, including memory loss, disorientation, and the gradual loss of self. This topic forms the foundation of the narrative, showing how the disease affects not only Alice but also her family and professional life.
pieces.about: Early-onset Alzheimer's disease is a rare form of Alzheimer's that affects people under the age of 65. It can present atypically, with symptoms that differ from those of late-onset Alzheimer's. Early-onset Alzheimer's can also progress faster than late-onset.

pieces.name: Easter
pieces.about: Easter, also called Pascha (Aramaic, Greek, Latin) or Resurrection Sunday, is a Christian festival and cultural holiday commemorating the resurrection of Jesus from the dead, described in the New Testament as having occurred on the third day of his burial following his crucifixion by the Romans at Calvary c. 30 AD.

English is also the standard language in many fields, including international business, computer coding, and higher education

pieces.name: Enthusiasm
pieces.about: Enthusiasm refers to a strong and passionate feeling of excitement, eagerness, and interest towards something or someone. It involves a positive and energetic attitude characterized by enthusiasm, optimism, and a sense of vitality.

pieces.name: Estrogen replacement therapy (ERT)
pieces.about: Estrogen replacement therapy (ERT) is a treatment that increases the amount of estrogen in the body to help relieve symptoms of menopause. It can also help prevent osteoporosis and lower the risk of breast cancer in postmenopausal women

pieces.name: Euphoria
pieces.about: A feeling of intense happiness and excitement.

pieces.name: Exercise
pieces.about: Exercise is physical activity that enhances or maintains fitness and overall health. It is performed for various reasons, including weight loss or maintenance, to aid growth and improve strength, develop muscles and the cardiovascular system, hone athletic skills, improve health, or simply for enjoyment.

pieces.name: Exhaustion
pieces.about: Feeling overtired, with low energy and a strong desire to sleep that interferes with normal daily activities.

pieces.name: Eye contact
pieces.about: Eye contact is a form of nonverbal communication and can have a large influence on social behavior.

pieces.name: Faith

pieces.name: Family Dynamics
pieces.sentence: (Page 6) Alice’s diagnosis has a profound impact on her family, particularly her husband, John, and her children, Anna, Tom, and Lydia. The novel examines how each family member copes with Alice’s illness, showcasing the strain, grief, and love that emerge as they navigate the challenges of caring for her and adapting to her changing abilities.
pieces.about: The patterns of relationship within a family - roles, alliances, conflicts and affection - and how they shape each member.

pieces.name: Feeling safe
pieces.about: Feeling safe is a fundamental human need, essential for both mental and physical well-being. It is the sense of security and freedom from fear or anxiety, allowing individuals to thrive and function optimally in their environment. The significance of feeling safe cannot be overstated, as it directly impacts stress responses, influencing overall health and happiness.

pieces.name: Fertility
pieces.about: Fertility is the ability to have babies or to reproduce. When fertility rates in a community increase, more babies are born. Fertility is the quality of a human's ability to produce offspring, which is dependent on age, health, and other factors.

pieces.name: Football (sport)
pieces.about: Football is a family of team sports that involve, to varying degrees, kicking a ball to score a goal. Unqualified, the word football generally means the form of football that is the most popular where the word is used. Sports commonly called football include association football ; Australian rules football; Gaelic football; gridiron football ; International rules football; rugby league football; and rugby union football. These various forms of football share, to varying degrees, common origins and are known as "football codes".

pieces.name: Fruit picking
pieces.about: Fruit picking or fruit harvesting is a seasonal activity that occurs during harvest time in areas with fruit growing wild or being farmed in orchards. Some farms market "You-Pick" for orchards, such as the tradition of Apple and Orange picking in North America, as a form of value-add agritourism.

also.title: The Little Mouse, the Red Ripe Strawberry, and the Big Hungry Bear

pieces.name: Getting lost
pieces.about: Unable to find one's way; not knowing one's whereabouts.

pieces.name: Goal Setting
pieces.about: Goal setting is the process of defining and working towards specific, measurable, and achievable goals within a set time frame. It's a fundamental practice that can help people and organizations stay motivated, track progress, and achieve success.

pieces.name: Golf
pieces.about: Golf is a club-and-ball sport in which players use various clubs to hit a ball into a series of holes on a course in as few strokes as possible.

also.title: Bomb: The Race to Build and Steal the World's Most Dangerous Weapon

pieces.name: Grandchild
pieces.about: A child of one's son or daughter.

also.title: Knuffle Bunny Free: An Unexpected Diversion

pieces.name: Growing up
pieces.about: The years of moving from early childhood toward adulthood, and the changes in body, mind, independence and relationships along the way.

also.title: Tales of a Fourth Grade Nothing
Knuffle Bunny Free: An Unexpected Diversion
When I was little: A four-year-old's memoir of her youth.

pieces.name: Hallucination
pieces.about: A perception of having seen, heard, touched, tasted, or smelled something that wasn't actually there.

pieces.name: Health
pieces.about: The condition of the body and mind, illness and recovery, and how sickness affects people's lives.

pieces.name: High School
pieces.about: A high school is a secondary school, where teenagers are educated before starting college or getting jobs.

also.title: Bomb: The Race to Build and Steal the World's Most Dangerous Weapon

pieces.name: History
pieces.about: History is the study of past events, particularly in human affairs, encompassing a wide range of disciplines, methodologies, and perspectives. It seeks to understand how societies, cultures, and individuals have evolved over time, influencing the present and shaping the future.

also.title: Bomb: The Race to Build and Steal the World's Most Dangerous Weapon

pieces.name: Hot Flash
pieces.about: A hot flash is the sudden feeling of warmth in the upper body, which is usually most intense over the face, neck and chest. Your skin might redden, as if you're blushing. A hot flash can also cause sweating. If you lose too much body heat, you might feel chilled afterward.

pieces.name: Hygiene
pieces.about: Hygiene is the practice of keeping yourself and your surroundings clean, especially in order to prevent illness or the spread of diseases.

pieces.name: Identity
pieces.about: The question of who a person is - what makes them themselves, where they belong, and how they come to know it.

also.title: What if the Zebras Lost Their Stripes?

pieces.name: Insomnia
pieces.about: Insomnia is a sleep disorder that makes it hard to fall asleep, stay asleep, or get quality sleep. It can cause you to feel tired during the day and interfere with your daily activities.

pieces.name: Intelligence quotient (IQ)
pieces.about: An intelligence quotient (IQ) is a total score derived from a set of standardized tests or subtests designed to assess human intelligence. Originally, IQ was a score obtained by dividing a person's mental age score, obtained by administering an intelligence test, by the person's chronological age, both expressed in terms of years and months. The resulting fraction (quotient) was multiplied by 100 to obtain the IQ score. For modern IQ tests, the raw score is transformed to a normal distribution with mean 100 and standard deviation 15. This results in approximately two-thirds of the population scoring between IQ 85 and IQ 115 and about 2 percent each above 130 and below 70.

pieces.name: Intrauterine insemination (IUI)
pieces.about: IUI is a fertility treatment procedure where washed sperm is directly inserted into the uterus to facilitate fertilization.

pieces.name: In vitro
pieces.about: In vitro studies are performed with microorganisms, cells, or biological molecules outside their normal biological context. Colloquially called "test-tube experiments", these studies in biology and its subdisciplines are traditionally done in labware such as test tubes, flasks, Petri dishes, and microtiter plates. Studies conducted using components of an organism that have been isolated from their usual biological surroundings permit a more detailed or more convenient analysis than can be done with whole organisms; however, results obtained from in vitro experiments may not fully or accurately predict the effects on a whole organism. In contrast to in vitro experiments, in vivo studies are those conducted in living organisms, including humans, known as clinical trials, and whole plants.

pieces.name: Irritability
pieces.about: Irritability is a state of being easily annoyed or angered, often in response to small things. It can be characterized by feelings of tension, touchiness, or being on edge. People who are irritable may have a short temper and react harshly, such as by snapping at others.

pieces.name: Knowledge
pieces.about: Facts, information, and skills acquired by a person through experience or education; the theoretical or practical understanding of a subject.

also.title: Bomb: The Race to Build and Steal the World's Most Dangerous Weapon
How I Built This - Wikipedia: Jimmy Wales
Journey to the Center of the Earth

pieces.name: Law School
pieces.about: A law school is a professional school or department of a college or university that specializes in legal education. Many people attend law school to become lawyers, judges, or other legal professionals.

pieces.name: Lewy Body Dementia
pieces.about: Lewy Body is a type of dementia caused by abnormal deposits of protein clumps in the brain. It can interfere with cognitive, motor skills and brain function. It is the second most common type of dementia.

pieces.name: Linguistics
pieces.about: The scientific study of language and its structure, including the study of morphology, syntax, phonetics, and semantics.

pieces.name: Logic
pieces.about: Logic is a system of principles that uses reason to determine if a conclusion is true or untrue. A person using logic will come to a generalized conclusion by looking at the given information and making an inference based on that data.

also.title: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe

pieces.name: Long distance relationship
pieces.about: A "long distance relationship" refers to a relationship where two partners live far apart from each other, making it difficult to see one another regularly, often relying on communication methods like phone calls, video chats, and texting to maintain their connection.

pieces.name: Long term memory
pieces.about: Long-term memory is the ability to store information and experiences for extended periods of time. It's a part of the Atkinson–Shiffrin memory model, which also includes sensory memory and short-term memory.

pieces.name: Long term plan
pieces.about: A long-term plan is a strategy that involves setting goals and outlining steps to achieve them over a significant period of time, usually five to twenty years. Long-term plans are characterized by their focus on big-picture objectives that require sustained effort over an extended period.

pieces.name: Make a decision
pieces.about: Making a decision is the act or process of selecting a course of action from several alternatives.

also.title: Bomb: The Race to Build and Steal the World's Most Dangerous Weapon
Knuffle Bunny Free: An Unexpected Diversion

pieces.name: Mammogram
pieces.about: A mammogram is an X-ray examination of the breast. It is used to detect and diagnose breast disease in women who either have breast problems, such as a lump, pain, or nipple discharge, as well as for women who have no breast complaints.

pieces.name: Marriage
pieces.about: Marriage is a legally and socially recognized union between two people, also known as spouses, that establishes rights and obligations.

also.title: Lemony Snicket's A Series of Unfortunate Events

pieces.name: Mathematics
pieces.about: Mathematics is an area of knowledge that includes the topics of numbers, formulas and related structures, shapes and the spaces in which they are contained, and quantities and their changes.

also.title: Bomb: The Race to Build and Steal the World's Most Dangerous Weapon
How I Built This - Wikipedia: Jimmy Wales
Rooster's Off to See the World
The Enigma Girls: How Ten Teenagers Broke Ciphers, Kept Secrets, and Helped Win World War II

pieces.name: Mechanism of Language
pieces.about: Language mechanisms include the rules and systems that govern how language is written and spoken, as well as the processes involved in language comprehension and acquisition

pieces.name: Medical School
pieces.about: A medical school is a professional school that teaches medicine and awards a degree to physicians. Medical school typically lasts four years, but students usually complete a residency and possibly a fellowship after that.

pieces.name: Medical (sick) leave
pieces.about: Sick leave is paid time off from work that workers can use to stay home to address their health needs without losing pay. It differs from paid vacation time or time off work to deal with personal matters, because sick leave is intended for health-related purposes. Sick leave can include a mental health day and taking time away from work to go to a scheduled doctor's appointment. Some policies also allow paid sick time to be used to care for sick family members, or to address health and safety needs related to domestic violence or sexual assault. Menstrual leave is another type of time off work for a health-related reason, but it is not always paid.

pieces.name: Medical Treatment (Therapy)
pieces.about: A therapy or medical treatment is the attempted remediation of a health problem, usually following a medical diagnosis.

pieces.name: Meditation
pieces.about: Meditation is a practice that involves training the mind to focus and redirect thoughts. It is often used to promote relaxation, build internal energy, and develop compassion, patience, and concentration.

also.title: Glad Monster, sad monster: a book about feelings
If I Could Turn Back Time

pieces.name: Menopause
pieces.sentence: Page 14- Alice reflects on her age and not yet experiencing hot flashes or night sweats.
pieces.about: Menopause is a point in time 12 months after a woman's last period. The years leading up to that point, when women may have changes in their monthly cycles, hot flashes, or other symptoms, are called the menopausal transition or perimenopause. The menopausal transition most often begins between ages 45 and 55.

pieces.name: Menstruation
pieces.about: Menstruation is the regular discharge of blood and mucosal tissue from the inner lining of the uterus through the vagina. The menstrual cycle is characterized by the rise and fall of hormones. Menstruation is triggered by falling progesterone levels and is a sign that pregnancy has not occurred.

pieces.name: Mental Health
pieces.about: Mental health refers to a person's overall psychological well-being, including their emotional, cognitive, and social functioning. It encompasses how individuals think, feel, and behave, as well as their ability to cope with stress, manage emotions, and navigate the challenges of life.

pieces.name: Mental Map
pieces.about: A mental map is a person's subjective representation of a place or area, based on their experiences, beliefs, and assumptions.

pieces.name: Mexican food
pieces.about: Mexican cuisine consists of the cooking cuisines and traditions of the modern country of Mexico. Its earliest roots lie in Mesoamerican cuisine. Mexican cuisine ingredients and methods begin with the first agricultural communities such as the Olmec and Maya who domesticated maize, created the standard process of nixtamalization, and established their foodways. Successive waves of other Mesoamerican groups brought with them their cooking methods. These included: the Teotihuacanos, Toltec, Huastec, Zapotec, Mixtec, Otomi, Purépecha, Totonac, Mazatec, Mazahua, and Nahua. With the Mexica formation of the multi-ethnic Triple Alliance, culinary foodways became infused.

pieces.name: Migraine
pieces.about: A type of headache characterized by severe, throbbing pain that typically occurs on one side of the head. It can also be accompanied by other symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, sensitivity to light and sound, and fatigue.

pieces.name: Mindfulness
pieces.about: Mindfulness is the cognitive skill, usually developed through meditation, of sustaining meta-attention of the contents of one's own mind in the present moment.

pieces.name: Missing being part of something
pieces.sentence: Page 285- Alice let's John know how she is feeling.

pieces.name: Molecular etiology of Alzheimer's
pieces.about: The molecular etiology of Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by the abnormal accumulation of proteins in the brain, including amyloid and tau.

pieces.name: Mood
pieces.about: In psychology, a mood is an affective state. In contrast to emotions or feelings, moods are less specific, less intense and less likely to be provoked or instantiated by a particular stimulus or event. Moods are typically described as having either a positive or negative valence. In other words, people usually talk about being in a good mood or a bad mood. There are many different factors that influence mood, and these can lead to positive or negative effects on mood.

also.title: Glad Monster, sad monster: a book about feelings

pieces.name: Mortality
pieces.about: Mortality refers to the quality or state of being a person or thing that is alive and therefore certain to die. It can also refer to the death of a person, animal, etc.. Mortality is often expressed in the form of mortality rate, which is the number of deaths due to an illness divided by the total population at that time

pieces.name: Music
pieces.about: Music is generally defined as the art of arranging sound to create some combination of form, harmony, melody, rhythm, or otherwise expressive content.

also.title: The Story of the Trapp Family Singers

pieces.name: Needy
pieces.about: Being ``needy'' typically refers to a state of excessive dependence on others for emotional support, validation, or attention.

pieces.name: Nervous of forgetting people
pieces.sentence: “You're so beautiful," said Alice. "I'm afraid of looking at you and not knowing who you are." This quote is talking about how if she starts to forget people, she'll feel bad because she loves them.

pieces.name: Networking (business)
pieces.about: Business networking is the practice of building relationships with individuals and businesses for professional purposes. It involves the strategic exchange of information and resources to create connections that can be mutually beneficial. Business networking can be conducted in person, online, or through a combination of both. Through repeated interactions, companies create deeper connections. This encourages knowledge exchange, mutual adaptation, and a commitment of resources, which can be both financial and social, to one another.

pieces.name: Nobel Prize
pieces.about: The Nobel Prizes are five separate prizes awarded to those who, during the preceding year, have conferred the greatest benefit to humankind, as established by the 1895 will of Swedish chemist, engineer, and industrialist Alfred Nobel, in the year before he died. Prizes were first awarded in 1901 by the Nobel Foundation. Nobel's will indicated that the awards should be granted in the fields of Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or Medicine, Literature, and Peace. A sixth prize for Economic Sciences, endowed by Sweden's central bank, Sveriges Riksbank, and first presented in 1969, is also frequently included, as it is also administered by the Nobel Foundation. The Nobel Prizes are widely regarded as the most prestigious awards available in their respective fields.

pieces.name: Ocean
pieces.about: An ocean is a very large expanse of sea, in particular each of the main areas into which the sea is divided geographically.

also.title: To Someone from A Warm Climate (Uiscefhuaraithe)

pieces.name: Overmedication
pieces.about: Overmedication describes the excessive use of over-the-counter or prescription medicines for a person. Overmedication can have harmful effects, such as non-adherence or interactions with multiple prescription drugs.

pieces.name: Panic
pieces.about: Panic is a sudden sensation of fear, which is so strong as to dominate or prevent reason and logical thinking, replacing it with overwhelming feelings of anxiety, uncertainty and frantic agitation consistent with a fight-or-flight reaction.

pieces.name: Parenting
pieces.about: Parenting or child rearing promotes and supports the physical, cognitive, social, emotional, and educational development from infancy to adulthood. Parenting refers to the intricacies of raising a child and not exclusively for a biological relationship.

pieces.name: Peer Review
pieces.about: Peer review is the evaluation of work by one or more people with similar competencies as the producers of the work. It functions as a form of self-regulation by qualified members of a profession within the relevant field.

pieces.name: Pension (Retirement savings)
pieces.about: A pension is a fund into which amounts are paid regularly during an individual's working career, and from which periodic payments are made to support the person's retirement from work.

pieces.name: Perseverance
pieces.about: Persistence in doing something despite difficulty or delay in achieving success.

The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild

pieces.name: Phone conversations
pieces.sentence: Page 94- Alice finds it difficult to have a conversation with Lydia over the phone without the aid of visual cues.

pieces.name: Phosphorylation
pieces.about: In biochemistry, phosphorylation is the attachment of a phosphate group to a molecule or an ion. This process and its inverse, dephosphorylation, are common in biology. Protein phosphorylation often activates many enzymes.

pieces.name: Political Science
pieces.about: Political science is the scientific study of politics, power, and governance. It involves analyzing political behavior, thought, activities, and the laws and constitutions that are associated with them. Political science also examines political ideas, ideologies, institutions, policies, processes, and groups.

pieces.name: Politics
pieces.about: How power is gained and used in a society, and how laws, governments and rulers affect people's lives.

also.title: Bomb: The Race to Build and Steal the World's Most Dangerous Weapon

pieces.name: Pregnancy
pieces.sentence: Page 30- Anna and Charlie are looking to start a family.
pieces.about: Pregnancy is the period of time when a fetus develops in a woman's uterus, and it typically lasts about 40 weeks, or just over 9 months. Pregnancy is divided into three trimesters, each lasting about 13 weeks.

pieces.name: Preventative care (medical check up)
pieces.about: Preventive care includes things such as regular check-ups, screenings and immunizations.

pieces.name: Progressive disease
pieces.about: A progressive illness or disease is a medical condition that worsens over time. This means that the symptoms and effects of the disease gradually become more severe.

pieces.name: Psycholinguistics
pieces.about: The study of the relationships between linguistic behavior and psychological processes, including the process of language acquisition.

pieces.name: Public speaking
pieces.about: Public speaking is the act of delivering a speech or presentation to a live audience. It can be formal or staged, but impromptu speeches are also common. The purpose of public speaking can be to inform, motivate, celebrate, entertain, or persuade

pieces.name: Pursuit
pieces.about: The action of following or pursuing someone or something

also.title: Percy Jackson & the Olympians: The Lightning Thief

pieces.name: Radiation (Therapy)
pieces.about: Radiation therapy or radiotherapy is a treatment using ionizing radiation, generally provided as part of cancer therapy to either kill or control the growth of malignant cells. It is normally delivered by a linear particle accelerator. Radiation therapy may be curative in a number of types of cancer if they are localized to one area of the body, and have not spread to other parts. It may also be used as part of adjuvant therapy, to prevent tumor recurrence after surgery to remove a primary malignant tumor. Radiation therapy is synergistic with chemotherapy, and has been used before, during, and after chemotherapy in susceptible cancers. The subspecialty of oncology concerned with radiotherapy is called radiation oncology. A physician who practices in this subspecialty is a radiation oncologist.

pieces.name: Repetitive motor disturbances
pieces.about: Repetitive motor disturbances, also known as motor stereotypies or stereotypic movement disorder, are involuntary, rhythmic, and predictable movements that occur repeatedly and seem to have no purpose. They can involve the hands, arms, or the whole body, and can include behaviors like head nodding, rocking, or hand flapping.

pieces.name: Restlessness
pieces.about: The quality of being unwilling or unable to stay still or to be quiet and calm, because you are worried or bored

pieces.name: Retirement
pieces.about: Retirement is the withdrawal from one's position or occupation or from one's active working life. A person may also semi-retire by reducing work hours or workload. Many people choose to retire when they are elderly or incapable of doing their job for health reasons.

pieces.name: Roman Clanedar
pieces.about: The Roman calendar was the calendar used by the Roman Kingdom and Roman Republic. Although the term is primarily used for Rome's pre-Julian calendars, it is often used inclusively of the Julian calendar established by Julius Caesar in 46 BC.

pieces.name: Running
pieces.about: Running is the activity of moving fast on foot, especially as a sport.

also.title: Spongebob Squarepants: Battle for Bikini Bottom Rehydrated

pieces.name: Sabbatical
pieces.about: A period of time during which someone does not work at his or her regular job and is able to rest, travel, do research, etc.

pieces.name: Self-Publishing
pieces.about: Self-publishing is the publication of media by its author at their own cost, without the involvement of a publisher.

pieces.name: Semantics
pieces.about: Semantics is the study of meaning in language, including how words and phrases get their meaning, and how the meaning of a complex expression is dependent on its parts.

pieces.name: Sibling interactions
pieces.about: The ways brothers and sisters get along, support, tease and compete with each other.

also.title: A Series of Unfortunate Events (TV series)
Lemony Snicket's A Series of Unfortunate Events
The War That Saved My Life

pieces.name: Sibling Rivalry
pieces.about: The conflict that can occur between brothers and sisters within a family. It is a natural and common dynamic that arises from the close proximity and shared resources among siblings, as well as from differences in personalities, temperaments, and levels of parental attention.

also.title: Tales of a Fourth Grade Nothing
When Sophie Gets Angry-Really, Really Angry...

pieces.name: Side effect
pieces.about: In medicine, a side effect is an effect of the use of a medicinal drug or other treatment, usually adverse but sometimes beneficial, that is unintended. Herbal and traditional medicines also have side effects.

pieces.name: Sleep
pieces.about: Sleep is a normal body process that allows your body and brain to rest. It is essential for physical, mental, and emotional health. During sleep, the body has a chance to rest and recover, and the brain processes memories. Sleep occurs in cycles, with each cycle lasting about 90 minutes on average.

pieces.name: Sleep deprivation
pieces.about: Sleep deprivation occurs when an individual fails to get the amount of sleep that they need. Sleep deprivation can occur due to various lifestyle, work and environmental factors.

pieces.name: Socialism
pieces.about: Socialism is a socio-economic and political ideology advocating for collective ownership and democratic control of the means of production, distribution, and exchange. It aims to create a society characterized by social and economic equality, where wealth and resources are distributed more equitably among the population. Socialism seeks to address issues such as poverty, inequality, and exploitation by promoting public ownership of key industries, social welfare programs, and democratic decision-making processes. While there are various interpretations and implementations of socialism, the fundamental principle is the prioritization of collective welfare and the reduction of class-based disparities in society.

pieces.name: Squash (sport)
pieces.about: Squash, sometimes called squash rackets, is a racket sport played by two (singles) or four players (doubles) in a four-walled court with a small, hollow, rubber ball. The players alternate in striking the ball with their rackets onto the playable surfaces of the four walls of the court. The objective of the game is to hit the ball in such a way that the opponent is not able to play a valid return. There are about 20 million people who play squash regularly world-wide in over 185 countries. The governing body of squash, the World Squash Federation (WSF), is recognized by the International Olympic Committee (IOC), and the sport will be included in the Olympic Games, starting with the 2028 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles. The Professional Squash Association (PSA) organizes the pro tour.

also.title: Bomb: The Race to Build and Steal the World's Most Dangerous Weapon

pieces.name: Stamina (Endurance)
pieces.about: Endurance is the ability of an organism to exert itself and remain active for a long period of time, as well as its ability to resist, withstand, recover from and have immunity to trauma, wounds, or fatigue.

pieces.name: Stroke
pieces.about: Stroke is a medical condition in which poor blood flow to a part of the brain causes cell death. There are two main types of stroke: ischemic, due to lack of blood flow, and hemorrhagic, due to bleeding. Both cause parts of the brain to stop functioning properly.

pieces.name: Stubbornness
pieces.about: Difficult to persuade, convince, or move. It can also mean having a firm idea or purpose or being determined.

pieces.name: Suicide
pieces.about: Taking one’s own life, the despair that can lead to it, and the help and hope that can prevent it.

also.title: A Tale for the Time Being

pieces.name: Sunset
pieces.about: Sunset is the disappearance of the Sun at the end of the Sun path, below the horizon of the Earth due to its rotation. As viewed from everywhere on Earth, it is a phenomenon that happens approximately once every 24 hours, except in areas close to the poles. The equinox Sun sets due west at the moment of both the spring and autumn equinoxes. As viewed from the Northern Hemisphere, the Sun sets to the northwest in the spring and summer, and to the southwest in the autumn and winter; these seasons are reversed for the Southern Hemisphere.

pieces.name: Superstition
pieces.about: A widely held but unjustified belief in supernatural causation leading to certain consequences of an action or event, or a practice based on such a belief.

also.title: A Red Herring Without Mustard: a Flavia de Luce mystery

pieces.name: Surgery
pieces.about: Surgery is a medical specialty that uses manual and instrumental techniques to diagnose or treat pathological conditions, to alter bodily functions, to reconstruct or improve aesthetics and appearance, or to remove unwanted tissues or foreign bodies.

pieces.name: Survival
pieces.about: To continue to live or exist, especially after coming close to dying or being destroyed or after being in a difficult or threatening situation.

also.title: Coral Reef Hideaway: The Story of a Clown Anemonefish
Journey to the Center of the Earth

pieces.name: Tennis (sport)
pieces.about: Tennis is a racket sport that is played either individually against a single opponent (singles) or between two teams of two players each (doubles). Each player uses a tennis racket strung with a cord to strike a hollow rubber ball covered with felt over or around a net and into the opponent's court. The object of the game is to manoeuvre the ball in such a way that the opponent is not able to play a valid return. The player unable to return the ball validly will not gain a point, while the opposite player will.

pieces.name: Thesis
pieces.about: A long piece of writing that presents original research, submitted for a university degree.

pieces.name: Time
pieces.sentence: Page 71- Alice is told by her neurologist that taking the drugs cab help by her as much time as possible.

also.title: Bomb: The Race to Build and Steal the World's Most Dangerous Weapon
If I Could Turn Back Time

pieces.name: Toast (drinking)
pieces.about: A toast is a ritual during which a drink is taken as an expression of honor or goodwill. It is to wish a person future health, happiness, and success and ask others to raise their glasses and join in a drink.

pieces.name: Toilet (potty)training
pieces.about: The process of training someone, particularly a toddler or infant, to use the toilet for urination and defecation.

pieces.name: Training
pieces.about: Training is teaching, or developing in oneself or others, any skills and knowledge or fitness that relate to specific useful competencies. Training has specific goals of improving one's capability, capacity, productivity and performance.

pieces.name: Victim
pieces.about: A casualty, as a term in military usage, is a person in military service, combatant or non-combatant, who becomes unavailable for duty due to any of several circumstances, including death, injury, illness, missing, capture or desertion.

pieces.name: Wandering
pieces.about: Wandering occurs when a person with dementia roams around and becomes lost or confused about their location. It is a common behavior that can cause great risk for the person, and is often the major priority for caregivers. It is estimated to be the most common form of disruption from people with dementia within institutions. Although it occurs in several types of dementia, wandering is especially common in people with Alzheimer's disease (AD). People with dementia often wander because they are stressed, looking for someone or something, attending to basic needs, engaging in past routines, or with visual-spatial problems. Other times, they may wander without aim at all.

pieces.name: Alienation
pieces.about: The state or experience of being isolated from a group or an activity to which one should belong or in which one should be involved.

pieces.name: Control
pieces.sentence: (Page 10) Throughout the novel, Alice struggles to maintain control over her life in the face of an illness that is robbing her of her autonomy. This theme is symbolized in her decision to create a plan for suicide when she feels her life is no longer worth living. The contrast between Alice’s once-commanding control over her life and her increasing powerlessness underscores the profound emotional toll of the disease.
pieces.about: Control is a multifaceted concept that plays a crucial role in various aspects of life, from personal self-regulation to organizational management and technological systems. Effective control mechanisms enhance efficiency, safety, and well-being, while ethical considerations ensure that control is exercised responsibly and equitably. Understanding and balancing control across different contexts helps in achieving desired outcomes while promoting autonomy, fairness, and mutual respect.

also.title: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest

pieces.name: Empathy
pieces.about: The ability to understand and share the feelings of another.

also.title: Glad Monster, sad monster: a book about feelings

What if the Zebras Lost Their Stripes?

pieces.name: Hope
pieces.sentence: (Page 59) Despite the bleakness of Alice’s diagnosis, there are moments of hope and resilience throughout the novel. Alice’s relationship with Lydia, in particular, exemplifies the theme of finding connection and meaning, even in the face of an incurable disease. The novel also offers hope in the possibility of medical research and the strength found in family bonds.
pieces.about: Hope is an optimistic state of mind that is based on an expectation of positive outcomes with respect to events and circumstances in one's life or the world at large.

Black Horse and the Cherry Tree
If I Could Turn Back Time
Star Wars: Episode IV - A New Hope

pieces.name: Passage of Time
pieces.about: The passage of time is a phrase that describes the process of time going past. It is not a physical thing, but an abstract concept that can be imagined as a flow from future to present to past. The passage of time can be measured in various units, such as minutes, days, years, etc..

also.title: A Tale for the Time Being
If I Could Turn Back Time
Knuffle Bunny Free: An Unexpected Diversion

pieces.name: Social change
pieces.about: Social change is the alteration of the social order of a society which may include changes in social institutions, social behaviors or social relations.

pieces.name: The Search for Meaning
pieces.about:
The search for meaning is a fundamental aspect of the human experience, encompassing the quest to understand life's purpose, significance, and one's place in the world. This journey often involves exploring philosophical, spiritual, and existential questions to find a sense of direction and fulfillment.

Key aspects of the search for meaning include:

Existential Questions: The search for meaning often begins with asking deep, existential questions such as "Why am I here?", "What is the purpose of life?", and "What happens after death?". These questions drive individuals to seek answers and understand their existence.

Personal Values and Beliefs: Understanding one's core values and beliefs is central to finding meaning. These guiding principles help shape decisions, behaviors, and goals, providing a sense of purpose and direction.

Life Purpose: Identifying a life purpose involves discovering what one is passionate about and what brings a sense of fulfillment. This might include career aspirations, creative pursuits, relationships, or contributions to society.

Connection to Others: Meaning is often found through relationships and connections with others. Building strong, supportive relationships and contributing to the well-being of others can provide a profound sense of purpose.

Spirituality and Religion: For many, spirituality and religion offer a framework for understanding the meaning of life. These belief systems provide answers to existential questions and a sense of connection to something greater than oneself.

Personal Growth and Self-Discovery: The journey of self-discovery and personal growth is integral to finding meaning. This involves understanding oneself, developing one's potential, and continuously evolving through life's experiences.

Contribution and Service: Meaning can be derived from contributing to the greater good and serving others. Acts of kindness, volunteering, and working toward social justice and environmental sustainability can provide a deep sense of purpose.

Creativity and Expression: Engaging in creative activities and self-expression allows individuals to explore and articulate their inner thoughts and emotions, often leading to a greater understanding of themselves and their place in the world.

Mindfulness and Presence: Practicing mindfulness and being present in the moment can enhance the search for meaning. It involves appreciating the present, finding joy in everyday experiences, and understanding the transient nature of life.

Philosophical Exploration: Engaging with philosophical ideas and theories about the nature of existence, ethics, and the human condition can offer insights and perspectives that enrich the search for meaning.

Resilience and Adversity: Meaning is often forged through facing and overcoming adversity. Challenges and hardships can lead to personal growth and a deeper understanding of one's purpose and values.

The search for meaning is a personal and evolving journey that varies for each individual. It is influenced by cultural, social, and personal contexts and can change over time as one grows and experiences life. Ultimately, finding meaning is about creating a life that is aligned with one's true self, values, and passions, leading to a sense of fulfillment and contentment.

pieces.about:
A politician is an individual who is actively involved in politics, typically holding elected or appointed positions within government or political organizations. Politicians play a central role in shaping public policy, making decisions that affect society, and representing the interests of constituents or members of their political party.

Key aspects of being a politician include:

Public Service: Politicians are responsible for serving the public interest and addressing the needs and concerns of the communities they represent.
Policy Making: Politicians participate in the development, implementation, and evaluation of policies and legislation at local, regional, national, or international levels.
Campaigning: Politicians often engage in campaigning activities to seek election or re-election to public office, which may involve fundraising, canvassing, public speaking, and media outreach.
Representation: Politicians serve as representatives of their constituents or members of their political party, advocating for their interests, concerns, and priorities within government institutions.
Negotiation and Compromise: Politicians frequently engage in negotiation and compromise to build consensus, forge alliances, and advance their policy agendas in complex political environments.
Public Communication: Politicians communicate with the public through various channels, such as speeches, press releases, social media, and public appearances, to articulate their positions, explain policy proposals, and engage with constituents.

Politicians can hold a variety of positions, including:

Legislator: Serving in legislative bodies such as parliaments, congresses, or city councils, where they propose, debate, and vote on laws and policies.
Executive: Holding executive positions such as president, governor, mayor, or prime minister, where they oversee the implementation of laws and policies and manage government agencies and departments.
Judicial: In some systems, politicians may also hold judicial positions, such as judges or justices, responsible for interpreting and applying the law.
Party Leader: Leading political parties and shaping party platforms, strategies, and campaigns.

Politicians may belong to various political parties or movements, each with its own ideology, goals, and approaches to governance. They operate within legal and institutional frameworks, navigating political processes and dynamics to achieve their objectives and serve their constituents.

pieces.about: Spend time interacting with individuals who have Alzheimer’s or dementia. Activities like reading to them, assisting with simple tasks, or just engaging in conversation can offer firsthand insights into their daily experiences. It’s a powerful way to build empathy and make a direct impact.

pieces.name: Volunteering
pieces.sentence: Spending time with individuals who have Alzheimer’s or other forms of dementia can provide firsthand insight into the struggles of memory loss, cognitive decline, and the emotional toll of the disease. Volunteering at a memory care facility or with an Alzheimer’s organization can help foster empathy for both patients and their families.
pieces.about: Giving your time and help to a cause or to people in need, without being paid.

pieces.name: Walking
pieces.about: Move at a regular pace by lifting and setting down each foot in turn, never having both feet off the ground at once.

pieces.name: Word Games
pieces.about: These type of games help stimulate the brain and requires active thinking.

pieces.name: Dream Big Notebook: Lined 6x9 Journal to Self-Express Your Goals, Dreams and Aspirations
pieces.sentence: Journals and scrapbooks can be used to document memories, thoughts, or family histories. In Still Alice, memory is central, as Alice struggles with the loss of her cognitive abilities. A memory journal encourages reflection on personal memories and the role they play in shaping one’s identity.

pieces.name: Weighted Blanket
pieces.sentence: A weighted blanket can provide comfort and help alleviate anxiety, a common emotion experienced by individuals with Alzheimer’s and their caregivers. In Still Alice, both Alice and her family experience significant emotional stress as they come to terms with her diagnosis, and a weighted blanket offers calming, sensory support.

pieces.name: Asking For Help
pieces.sentence: Alice's journey shows the gradual necessity of accepting assistance, from initially hiding her symptoms to eventually relying on caregivers. The novel demonstrates that asking for help preserves dignity rather than diminishing it, especially through Alice's evolution from independent professor to someone who learns to accept support gracefully.

pieces.name: Building Relationships
pieces.sentence: The story explores how Alice's diagnosis both strains and strengthens relationships. Her connection with her youngest daughter Lydia deepens as they find new ways to relate beyond intellectual discourse, showing that meaningful relationships can transcend cognitive abilities.

pieces.name: I want to get better at communication
pieces.sentence: As Alice loses verbal fluency, the novel illustrates alternative forms of connection through touch, presence, and emotional understanding. Her struggle to find words and her family's efforts to interpret her needs demonstrate the importance of patience and creative communication strategies.

pieces.name: Crisis Management
pieces.sentence: The narrative follows the family's response to Alice's wandering episode and getting lost, showing how they develop safety protocols, use technology like GPS trackers, and create structured routines to manage emergencies while preserving Alice's autonomy as much as possible.

pieces.name: I want to get better at decision making
pieces.sentence: Alice's early decision to create instructions for her future self, including her controversial suicide plan, explores the complexity of making choices while cognitively intact for a future impaired self, raising questions about autonomy and advance directives.

pieces.name: Doctor visit
pieces.sentence: The novel details Alice's diagnostic journey, from initial dismissal of symptoms to neurological testing, showing the importance of advocacy, second opinions, and honest communication with healthcare providers about cognitive changes.

pieces.name: Emotions
pieces.sentence: Alice experiences the full spectrum from denial and anger to moments of peace, demonstrating that emotional capacity persists even as cognition declines. The family's varied emotional responses—John's denial, Anna's grief, Lydia's acceptance—normalize the complexity of feelings surrounding degenerative illness.

pieces.name: Family dynamics
pieces.sentence: The diagnosis reshuffles family roles as the accomplished mother becomes dependent on her children, John struggles between career and caregiving, and siblings navigate different coping styles, showing how illness transforms but doesn't destroy family bonds.

pieces.name: Future trajectory
pieces.sentence: Alice's academic future evaporates, but the novel explores redefining purpose and meaning beyond professional identity. Her trajectory shifts from planned retirement to an uncertain path, teaching adaptation to radically altered life expectations.

pieces.name: Harm prevention
pieces.sentence: The family implements practical safety measures like removing car keys, simplifying the home environment, and establishing routines, demonstrating proactive approaches to preventing accidents while maintaining quality of life.

pieces.name: Healthcare and making the right choices
pieces.sentence: The novel explores treatment options, clinical trials, and care decisions, showing how families must navigate limited options, weigh quality versus quantity of life, and make choices with incomplete information.

pieces.name: I want to make better choices
pieces.sentence: Alice's story illustrates prioritizing relationships over achievements, choosing presence over productivity, and selecting what matters most when time and capacity are limited.

pieces.name: Motivation
pieces.sentence: Despite her decline, Alice finds motivation in small goals like remembering her daughter's play or maintaining routines, showing that purpose can be redefined and scaled to match current abilities.

pieces.name: Obstacles
pieces.sentence: The novel presents cognitive barriers as daily obstacles—finding the bathroom, recognizing family members, completing sentences—and shows both successful adaptations and heartbreaking failures in overcoming them.

pieces.name: Parental expectation
pieces.sentence: Alice must release expectations for her children's achievements and accept their choices, particularly Lydia's acting career, while her children must adjust their expectations of their mother's role in their lives.

pieces.name: Paying attention and staying focused
pieces.sentence: The narrative captures Alice's increasing difficulty with attention, from losing track in lectures to being unable to follow conversations, demonstrating strategies like note-taking and environmental modifications to support focus.

pieces.name: Perseverance
pieces.sentence: Alice continues attempting to read, exercise, and engage with family despite repeated failures, embodying persistence even when progress is impossible, teaching that effort itself has value.

pieces.name: Physical and mental fitness
pieces.sentence: The novel shows Alice maintaining running routines and attempting cognitive exercises, illustrating how physical activity supports brain health and provides structure, though it cannot stop progression.

pieces.name: I want to get better at prioritization
pieces.sentence: As capabilities narrow, Alice and her family must constantly reprioritize, choosing essential activities over optional ones, and emotional connection over intellectual pursuits.

pieces.name: I want to get better at regulating behavior
pieces.sentence: Alice struggles with inappropriate responses and impulse control, while her family learns to redirect rather than correct, showing compassionate behavior management strategies.

pieces.name: Remembering
pieces.sentence: The core challenge of the novel, addressed through memory aids, repetition, emotional memory preservation, and ultimately accepting that identity persists beyond specific memories.

pieces.name: Responsibility balance
pieces.sentence: John and the children navigate caregiving responsibilities while maintaining their own lives, showing the delicate balance between duty and self-preservation, and the importance of shared responsibility.
